name: surfnterd/pricelabs-tracker
what_it_holds: Python/FastAPI/SQLite tool that, given a user's own PriceLabs API key, takes daily snapshots for a listing: recommended/base price and min-max cap flags, >20% price-change history, YoY booking pace (occupancy and revenue vs. same days-out last year, alerts at >10pp lag), 'neighborhood market comp' snapshots daily, 3 years of backfilled reservation history, and Airbnb/Booking.com channel-mix split. MIT licensed, 1 commit, 0 stars (low adoption/no track record). No sample data committed; requires the operator's own paid PriceLabs account to run.
why_useful: Shows the shape of PriceLabs' own-listing pace/YoY export (relevant to gap #2 style booking-pace concepts) but is single-listing telemetry, not a market panel, and needs a paid PriceLabs subscription to run.
size_hint: code only, snapshots kept locally by the operator, not in the repo
themes: Airbnb pricing tools and dynamic-pricing repos that embed market data (PriceLabs, Beyond, Wheelhouse style; open-source STR pricing with comps)
why_all: Shows the shape of PriceLabs' own-listing pace/YoY export (relevant to gap #2 style booking-pace concepts) but is single-listing telemetry, not a market panel, and needs a paid PriceLabs subscription to run.

This is the most direct hit on the theme: a working, open-source method for pulling PriceLabs' own market-comp and pacing data (the exact quantity gap #2 wants — realised/ comp occupancy and ADR for STRs from a market-data vendor) rather than another NYC-2019 rehash. Would need a team member's/partner's PriceLabs subscription to actually run.

name: airbnb-scraper (everythingscraper)
what_it_holds: Very small repo (0 stars, 2 commits) wrapping an Apify Actor that explicitly computes occupancy rate, ADR and RevPAR per listing from Airbnb's forward-looking 12-month calendar, plus day-by-day booking status/pricing for the full 12 months, listing amenities/images/coordinates/review counts, and optional full review text/host portfolio. README shows a worked sample row (Paris listing: 78% occupancy, EUR142.50 ADR, EUR111.15 RevPAR). No committed dataset; output goes to JSON via Apify (paid).
why_useful: A working method to derive occupancy/ADR/RevPAR comps directly from Airbnb calendars at scale (gap #2/#8-style comp data), but it operates by scraping airbnb.com itself — squarely the class of tool CONTEXT flags as a terms-of-service decision for a human, so this should be catalogued as method-only and NOT run.

name: gobnb
what_it_holds: Go-language port of the same author's Airbnb scraper (39 stars, 22 commits, MIT, updated Jul 2025). Extracts room-level listing data (price, check-in/out, images), and search results by geographic coordinates/zoom level, optimized for airbnb.com/rooms/[roomID] URLs.
why_useful: Same method family as pyairbnb; only useful if the desk ever needs a non-Python runtime. Not a new data source.

name: airbnb-scraper (digital-engineering, Scrapy)
what_it_holds: GPL-3.0 Scrapy spider (210 stars, updated Aug 2026, the highest-starred repo in this theme) for Airbnb search results. Exports via AirbnbScraperItem/FIELDS_TO_EXPORT (customizable in settings.py) to CSV/XLSX/Elasticsearch; README confirms name, description, review text and property ID fields at minimum, plus filterable search params (min/max price, checkin/checkout dates, neighborhoods, room types, weekly/monthly discount %). Author notes the project is 'no longer maintained' and exploring a simpler approach -- no committed sample data.
why_useful: Longest-running, most-starred open Airbnb search scraper; documents a discount-percentage field (weekly/monthly) that could proxy price elasticity/promotional intensity if ever run. Catalogue as method only.
